newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends off on post-FOMC relief.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends off on post-FOMC relief.

text.p: Mexico's overnight Cetes rate closed down 18 basis points at 29.15 percent on Wednesday after zigzagging through the session on thin volume.
Some traders put the late fall down to the Federal Open Market Committee's decision not to alter U.S. interest rates.

"(The FOMC meeting) removed some jitters from the market, but the market was sluggish even so. We've been waiting for a rally for days, but in the meanwhile, the market's been moving sideways in light trade," said a trader.
The overnight rate fluctuated between 29.80 and 29.10 percent during the session.
Traders said that lack of trading in term instruments was a sign of continuing uncertainty.
"You can tell there is still nervousness in the market. Dealers prefer to play it safe and that means holding the market up," said a money market analyst.
Secondary rates on 182-day Cetes were traded at 28.50 percent, compared to primary rates of 28.07 percent assigned at Tuesday night's auction.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile closed up 30 basis points at 30.80 percent.
Banco de Mexico earlier injected 5.155 billion pesos by auctioning three credits at 31.16, 31.70 and 32.08 percent.

Total credit maturities for Thursday were estimated at 2.502 billion pesos, although traders pointed out that the ensuing liquidity shortage could be offset by a surplus of 696 million pesos carried over from the primary auction.
